name: Pelican Drift Aquatics
full_legal_name: Pelican Drift Aquatics Corponation, Sovereign Marine Enterprise
sovereign_territory: The Drift Yards — a sovereign archipelago of 34 semi-permanent floating platforms anchored across Lake Huron and Lake Michigan, connected by a proprietary fast-transit waterway system. The largest platform, Pelican Prime, spans 4.2 kilometers and serves as the corponation's administrative capital. Total sovereign water-surface area claimed: approximately 900 square kilometers.
founding_story: Pelican Drift emerged from the ruins of the Great Lakes Water Authority following its privatization under the Meridian Compact's 2136 Resource Sovereignty Amendments. A joint venture between three Scandinavian infrastructure funds and a Chicago-based municipal water utility, it was initially tasked with maintaining potable water delivery to the megacity corridor. Within a decade, it had acquired sovereign status over the processing platforms, developed proprietary low-energy desalination membranes capable of processing microplastic-laden lake water at industrial scale, and pivoted from utility provider to resource corponation. Its founders have long since been diluted out of meaningful equity by successive capital raises.
security_force: The Warden Fleet — a 3,400-person maritime security force operating 67 armed patrol vessels, 12 submersible interdiction craft, and a network of underwater sensor arrays across claimed sovereign waters. The Warden Fleet has engaged in lethal force against unauthorized water extraction operations on 14 documented occasions since 2144. Cormorant Naval Systems has a standing contract to supply the Warden Fleet's heavier vessels.
key_detail: Pelican Drift holds the Meridian Compact's exclusive license for commercial freshwater extraction from Lakes Huron and Michigan through 2167. Every liter of potable water consumed by approximately 31 million corridor residents was processed by Pelican Drift infrastructure. The corponation has never publicly acknowledged that it deliberately slowed membrane technology rollout for three years to maintain scarcity pricing.
relationship_to_big_20: Full Big 20 member, ranked approximately 7th by total valuation. Pelican Drift is considered one of the 'untouchable' members because its product is non-substitutable — no competing corponation can realistically displace it from the water supply chain without triggering a humanitarian crisis that would destabilize the entire Meridian Compact framework.
full_text: Water is the oldest power in GLMZ, and Pelican Drift Aquatics holds it. The corponation's floating platform archipelago is one of the megacity corridor's most distinctive landmarks — a chain of industrial islands visible from the shore on clear days, their processing towers exhaling white vapor, their running lights reflecting in long lines across the dark lake water after nightfall. Life aboard the Drift Yards is its own subculture: roughly 12,000 people live permanently on the platforms, in a society organized around shift rotations, platform rank, and an intense in-group identity centered on the idea that Drift workers keep the city alive. They are not wrong. Pelican Drift's membrane processing technology is genuine intellectual property — its third-generation Clarity Membrane can extract potable water from lake inputs with a bacterial load 40 times higher than previous standards, a capability that became critically important as industrial runoff from corridor manufacturing zones degraded lake quality through the 2040s. The corponation also sells water futures on the Meridian Exchange, a practice that has made it extraordinarily wealthy and generated sustained public outrage, particularly during the dry summers of 2148 and 2150 when spot prices for residential water spiked to levels that pushed lower-tier corridor residents into dangerous rationing. Pelican Drift's public relations operation responds to these criticisms with infrastructure investment announcements and scholarship programs. Its pricing desk responds to nothing. The corponation is currently in a protracted territorial dispute with Crestfall Aquaculture over sovereign water-surface rights in Lake Huron's Saginaw Bay sector, a conflict that has involved three Warden Fleet interdictions of Crestfall vessels in the past 18 months.
